questions.text: CSS 2016 · Pair: Adverse / Averse — Which meaning fits “Adverse”?

options.A: A person who writes annals, i.e. year-by-year historical records
options.B: Strongly unwilling or opposed to something
options.C: A thickened, hardened area of skin caused by repeated friction
options.D: Harmful or unfavourable (used of conditions, effects, events)

questions.explanation:
Adverse: Harmful or unfavourable (used of conditions, effects, events). Sentence: "The adverse weather forced the pilot to land in Multan instead of Islamabad, because the fog made flying unsafe."
Averse: Strongly disliking or unwilling (used of a person's attitude: averse to). Sentence: "Being averse to crowds, Ali always shops early in the morning when the bazaar is empty."
Source: CSS 2016 English Precis & Composition (cssaspirants.pk).

questions.text: CSS 2016 · Pair: Altogether / All together — Which meaning fits “Altogether”?

options.A: Having only one spouse or mate at a time
options.B: Angry (archaic/literary adjective, used after a verb)
options.C: Gathered in one place at the same time
options.D: Completely, entirely; or on the whole

questions.explanation:
Altogether: Completely, entirely; or on the whole. Sentence: "The old bridge was altogether unsafe, so the authorities closed it to all traffic."
All together: Everyone or everything in one group or at the same time. Sentence: "The family sat all together around one table for the Eid dinner."
Source: CSS 2016 English Precis & Composition (cssaspirants.pk).

questions.text: CSS 2016 · Pair: Allude / Elude — Which meaning fits “Allude”?

options.A: To state something openly and explicitly
options.B: To refer to something indirectly, without naming it
options.C: A short quotation at the start of a book or chapter; an inscription on a building or statue
options.D: An underground room or vault beneath a church, used for burial

questions.explanation:
Allude: To refer to something indirectly, without naming it. Sentence: "Without naming anyone, the speaker alluded to the minister's broken promises, and the audience understood whom he meant."
Elude: To escape or avoid someone or something cleverly; to be hard to grasp. Sentence: "The thief eluded the police by slipping through a crowded alley."
Source: CSS 2016 English Precis & Composition (cssaspirants.pk).

questions.text: CSS 2016 · Pair: Braise / Braze — Which meaning fits “Braise”?

options.B: To grill food quickly over an open flame
options.C: A clever trick or stratagem meant to deceive (usually plural: wiles)
options.D: To cook food slowly in a little liquid in a covered pot

questions.explanation:
Braise: To cook food slowly in a little liquid in a covered pot. Sentence: "She braised the mutton for three hours over a low flame until it fell off the bone."
Braze: To join two pieces of metal using a melted alloy of copper and zinc (brass). Sentence: "The mechanic brazed the cracked copper pipe so the joint would no longer leak."
Source: CSS 2016 English Precis & Composition (cssaspirants.pk).

questions.text: CSS 2016 · Pair: Curb / Kerb — Which meaning fits “Curb”?

options.A: To restrain or keep something under control; a restraint
options.B: The raised stone edge of a pavement (British spelling)
options.C: To pretend to be affected by a feeling or state
options.D: A person who rides the leading near-side horse of a team drawing a carriage

questions.explanation:
Curb: To restrain or keep something under control; a restraint. Sentence: "The government raised interest rates to curb rising inflation."
Kerb: The raised stone edge between the pavement and the road (British spelling). Sentence: "The child waited on the kerb until the traffic light turned green before crossing."
Source: CSS 2016 English Precis & Composition (cssaspirants.pk).

questions.text: CSS 2016 · Pair: Faze / Phase — Which meaning fits “Faze”?

options.A: A deep, wide ditch, usually filled with water, around a castle or fort
options.C: To disturb or unsettle someone's composure
options.D: A distinct stage in a process or development

questions.explanation:
Faze: To disturb or unsettle someone's composure. Sentence: "The noisy hall did not faze the candidate; he answered every question calmly."
Phase: A distinct stage in a process of change or development. Sentence: "The first phase of the metro project covers the route from the airport to the city centre."
Source: CSS 2016 English Precis & Composition (cssaspirants.pk).

questions.text: CSS 2016 · Pair: Maybe / May be — Which meaning fits “Maybe”?

options.B: Something that has the possibility of being (verb phrase)
options.C: The killing of a wife by her husband
options.D: A story or deed of adventure, especially a heroic exploit (also 'geste')

questions.explanation:
Maybe: Perhaps; possibly (adverb, one word). Sentence: "Maybe it will rain tomorrow, so take an umbrella just in case."
May be: Verb phrase meaning 'might be' or 'is possibly'. Sentence: "The result may be announced on Friday if the committee finishes its work."
Source: CSS 2016 English Precis & Composition (cssaspirants.pk).

questions.text: CSS 2016, 2026 · Pair: Moat / Mote — Which meaning fits “Moat”?

options.A: A deep, wide ditch, usually filled with water, around a castle or fort
options.B: A period of time; during the time that
options.C: A person who leaves their own country to settle in another
options.D: A tiny particle or speck of dust

questions.explanation:
Moat: A deep, wide ditch, usually filled with water, around a castle or fort. Sentence: "The fort was surrounded by a moat, so attackers had to cross the water before reaching the walls."
Mote: A tiny speck, especially of dust. Sentence: "In the shaft of sunlight we could see every mote of dust floating in the air."
Source: CSS 2016, 2026 English Precis & Composition (cssaspirants.pk).
